Close to the Hebrew; “Consider” is rendered “Observe,” and the ant is referred to as “her.”
Close to the Hebrew; NASB renders “which has no commander” as “Which, having no chief.”
Close to the Hebrew; The second “its food” is rendered “her provision.”

Close to the Hebrew; “A traveler” is rendered “a vagabond,” and “a man of shield” as “an armed man.”
Close to the Hebrew; “Walking [with] crookedness of mouth” is rendered “walks with a false mouth,” and NASB adds “Is the one.”
Close to the Hebrew; “Scraping with his feet” is rendered “signals with his feet.”
Close to the Hebrew; “At every time” is rendered “continually,” and “contentions” as “strife.”

Close to the Hebrew; “Disgusting thing of his self” is rendered “an abomination to Him,” and NASB adds “Yes.”

Close to the Hebrew; The singular “it” is rendered “they,” and “it will speak” as “they will talk.”
Close to the Hebrew; “Instruction” (torah) is rendered “teaching,” and “rebukes of discipline” as “reproofs for discipline.”
Close to the Hebrew; “A woman of evil” is rendered “the evil woman,” and “a foreign woman” as “the adulteress.”

“For the price of a prostitute [one comes] to a round loaf of bread” is rendered “on account of a harlot one is reduced to a loaf of bread,” and “the wife of a man” as “an adulteress.” The meaning of the Hebrew is uncertain.
Close to the Hebrew; “Snatch up” is rendered “take.”
